logline: A paranoid, brilliant hacker working for a cybersecurity firm is recruited into a revolution - and discovers the most dangerous exploit is inside his own mind.

bollymeter.basis: Every episode of S1 holds 100% approval on RT - the most sustained critical run in the franchise's history. The hacking is technically credible, Rami Malek's performance is magnetic, and Sam Esmail's cinematic ambition was unlike anything on cable.

pull_quotes.text: Rami Malek is mesmerising in a debut season that is technically audacious, psychologically complex, and unlike anything else on television.

seasons.review_body: The debut season of Mr. Robot is the rare prestige television case where technical credibility and creative ambition reinforce each other. Sam Esmail hired actual hackers as consultants; the attacks on E Corp are accurate enough that cybersecurity firms circulated the episodes internally. But the technical realism would mean nothing without Rami Malek's Elliot Alderson - a performance of dissociation, paranoia, and buried pain that won Malek the Emmy and created television's most compelling anti-hero of the decade. The show's aesthetic - Kubrickian framing, deliberate dead space, handheld instability - functions as visual psychology. Every episode drew 100% on RT; critics who cover both film and television recognised Esmail as a genuinely cinematic filmmaker working in long form. Season 1 ends with a revelation that restructures everything the audience thought they understood.

episode_reviews.title: eps1.0_hellofriend.mov
episode_reviews.review_body: Mr. Robot Season 1 Episode 1 'eps1.0_hellofriend.mov' aired June 24, 2015 on USA Network as the premiere of a series that earned 100 percent on Rotten Tomatoes across every episode of its first season. IMDb audiences scored the series 8.7. The Rotten Tomatoes consensus called Rami Malek 'mesmerising in a debut that is technically audacious, psychologically complex, and unlike anything else on television.' The pilot introduces Elliot Alderson in a mode of direct viewer address that establishes an unreliable narrator contract without formally announcing it - the audience is brought inside Elliot's perspective while being given enough structural clues to suspect they should not fully trust it. Sam Esmail hired actual hackers as consultants; the E Corp attacks are technically credible in a way few television dramas attempt. The aesthetic - Kubrickian framing, deliberate dead space - is fully formed at episode one.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The pilot introduces Elliot Alderson - a cyber-security engineer, hacker, and unreliable narrator - in a mode of address that breaks the fourth wall while maintaining plausible deniability about how far Elliot's perception can be trusted. The show's aesthetic and ethical stance are both fully formed at episode one.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Elliot's direct address to the viewer: the show revealing its narrative contract and the discomfort that contract implies.

critic_note.text: Rami Malek is mesmerising in a debut that is technically audacious, psychologically complex, and unlike anything else on television.

episode_reviews.title: eps1.4_3xpl0its.wmv
episode_reviews.review_body: Mr. Robot Season 1 Episode 5 'eps1.4_3xpl0its.wmv' aired July 22, 2015 on USA Network as part of a debut season that earned 100 percent across all episodes on Rotten Tomatoes. IMDb audiences scored the series 8.7. The social engineering episode is the season's clearest demonstration of the show's technical credibility: the methods Elliot and Darlene use to infiltrate a target through psychological manipulation are accurate, the procedural logic is sound, and Sam Esmail directs the physical infiltration sequence with Kubrickian spatial precision. The episode also deepens the relationship between Elliot and Mr. Robot, whose influence and motives grow more ambiguous here than in any prior episode. The show's visual grammar - static wide frames, bodies positioned at the image's edges - is at its most formally disciplined.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The social engineering episode: Elliot and Darlene work a target through psychological manipulation. The show's technical credibility is at its most visible - the hacks are accurate, the logic is sound - while the character study deepens. Mr. Robot's influence over Elliot grows more complex.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The physical infiltration sequence - the show's most cinematic hour to this point, shot with Kubrickian precision.

episode_reviews.title: eps1.7_wh1ter0se.m4v
episode_reviews.review_body: Mr. Robot Season 1 Episode 8 'eps1.7_wh1ter0se.m4v' aired August 12, 2015 on USA Network as part of a debut season that earned 100 percent across all episodes on Rotten Tomatoes. IMDb audiences scored the series 8.7. The episode introduces Whiterose - BD Wong's character who exists simultaneously as a Dark Army hacker and as a formal presence in geopolitical machinery the show had been gesturing at peripherally. BD Wong's performance lands with immediate total authority: the first scene establishes the character's dual registers without explaining them. The meeting between Elliot and Whiterose expands the show's moral universe from personal paranoia to geopolitical scale, and the cartel's reach becomes visible for the first time. The episode recontextualises every prior antagonist in the show's world.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Whiterose introduction episode and a turning point in the show's mythology. BD Wong's performance is immediate and total: a character who exists in multiple registers simultaneously. The cartel's global scale becomes visible for the first time.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Whiterose and Elliot's first meeting - the scene that expands Mr. Robot's moral universe from personal paranoia to geopolitical conspiracy.

episode_reviews.title: eps1.9_zer0-day.avi
episode_reviews.review_body: Mr. Robot Season 1 Episode 10 'eps1.9_zer0-day.avi' aired September 2, 2015 on USA Network as the season finale of a series that earned 100 percent on Rotten Tomatoes across all first-season episodes. IMDb audiences scored the series 8.7. The A.V. Club called it 'a masterwork of misdirection and emotional truth.' The 5/9 hack - fsociety's planned revolution against E Corp - executes in the finale and delivers the spectacle the season promised. The episode's reputation rests on its final minutes: the revelation about Elliot's relationship to Mr. Robot restructures the entire season with information the show had placed correctly but obscured with precision. Critics noted the show played fair throughout - the clues were present but the misdirection was exact enough that a rewatch becomes a different viewing experience.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The 5/9 hack happens. The season finale delivers the revolution fsociety has been building toward, and then restructures the entire story in its final minutes. The revelation forces an immediate rewatch of the season with different eyes - and the show played fair throughout.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final revelation about Elliot's relationship to Mr. Robot - one of television's great unreliable-narrator payoffs.

critic_note.text: Mr. Robot's season finale is a masterwork of misdirection and emotional truth.

bollymeter.basis: 90% RT, critics average 7.85/10. The most polarising season: deliberately slow, structured around a formal deception that rewarded patient viewers and frustrated impatient ones. The critical consensus is kinder than the real-time viewer reaction.

pull_quotes.text: Season 2 is bold and demanding - a formal experiment that not all viewers will accept, but rewards those who do.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 is where the casual audience fell away and the committed audience got exactly what they signed up for. Esmail structures the season around Elliot's situation in a way that only reveals its shape in the final act - a formal deception requiring complete audience trust for episodes that seem to be going nowhere. The 90% RT reflects critics who read the show's intentions correctly; the viewer drop-off reflected an audience that didn't. The season-long exploration of Darlene, the fsociety aftermath, and the Dark Army's global reach deepens the world substantially. The 1.0 episode - shot in real time, on an '80s sitcom stage with a laugh track - is the season's formal peak and one of the strangest hours of television in 2016. In retrospect, S2 is essential architecture.
seasons.season_over_season: Deliberately paced to the point of testing loyalty, but the formal risks justify themselves in context of the full series arc.

bollymeter.basis: 92% RT, critics average 8.25/10. The season that rehabilitated the show's casual audience and delivered its most technically extraordinary episodes, including a 45-minute single-take episode.

pull_quotes.text: Season 3 is Mr. Robot at its most operatic - a return to form that delivers some of the most technically ambitious television ever produced.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 is where Mr. Robot reclaimed everyone who had wavered in S2. The single-take episode - Episode 5, 'Runtime Error' - is 45 minutes of continuous filming across the E Corp building, hacking in real time, intercut with action set-pieces. Esmail directed it himself and it stands alongside True Detective S1's tracking shot as a technical landmark. The fsociety endgame delivers the 5/9 hack consequences the show had been building toward; the Dark Army's motivations gain geopolitical scale. BD Wong's Whiterose is the season's secret weapon. Critics gave it 92%; audiences who had drifted back for S3 delivered the best real-time reception the show had since its debut. The writing sharpened because the architecture was fully visible.
seasons.season_over_season: The formal ambition of S2 lands in S3's execution - this is what the slow season was building toward.

bollymeter.basis: 96% RT, critics average 8.95/10 - the highest score since S1. Esmail delivered the ending he planned from the start, and the final two episodes are among the most emotionally complete series finales in prestige television.

pull_quotes.text: A finale season of rare integrity - Mr. Robot ends exactly as it promised, with formal daring and genuine emotional payoff.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 is the rarest outcome for an ambitious serialised drama: a planned ending that arrives exactly as intended and earns everything it claims. Esmail takes the show's psychological architecture - built across four seasons - and completes it with the same rigour the show applied to its hacking sequences. The penultimate episode is a silent film. The finale is one of the most discussed series conclusions since Breaking Bad's Felina, with critics and fans aligned that the revelation is not a trick but a structural inevitability the show had been pointing at from episode one. At 96% RT, S4 is the show's critical peak. The 8.8 IMDb score reflects audience consensus that Esmail honoured the contract. Mr. Robot is the prestige drama that most thoroughly rewards rewatching.
seasons.season_over_season: The planned ending delivered intact - the series closes with the confidence of a show that always knew where it was going.
